item.title: PHP PDO How to View Interpolated SQL Queries with Bound Parameters
item.description:
“PHP PDO How to View Interpolated SQL Queries with Bound Parameters”

How can a developer effectively inspect or retrieve the fully interpolated SQL query string when using PDO::prepare() and PDO::execute()?

Examining Interpolated SQL Queries in PDO

The core challenge is that the true, executed SQL command (template + values) is usually assembled on the database server, not on the client side (where your PHP code runs). This architecture prevents PDO from inherently exposing the final string. Several methods exist to work around this limitation, ranging from server-side logging to client-side interpolation functions.

item.title: PDO Error Handling: Exceptions vs ErrorInfo with PHP
item.description:
“PDO Error Handling: Exceptions vs ErrorInfo with PHP”

When interacting with databases using PHP’s PDO extension, robust error management is crucial for building reliable applications. This often involves deciding between PDO’s exception mode or utilizing the errorInfo() method. Let’s delve into the nuances and best practices.

The Role of PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE

The PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE attribute dictates how PDO handles errors. Setting it to PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION is a common and recommended approach. When an error occurs, PDO will throw a PDOException, allowing you to catch and handle it gracefully using try...catch blocks.

item.title: PDO rowCount() for SELECT: Best Practices and Alternatives
item.description:
“PDO rowCount() for SELECT: Best Practices and Alternatives”

When working with PHP’s PDO and executing SELECT queries, a common challenge arises: accurately determining the number of rows returned. While PDOStatement::rowCount() is the apparent method, its behavior with SELECT statements can be inconsistent across different database drivers. This post delves into the nuances, why rowCount() often falls short for SELECT queries, and presents robust alternatives for obtaining accurate row counts, ensuring efficient database interactions.
